stories.text: The Council House, designed by Thomas Cecil Howitt, opened in 1929 on the site of the old Exchange at the head of the Old Market Square.[^s1][^s1] The sculptor Joseph Else named the two stone lions on its steps Agamemnon and Menelaus.[^s1][^s1] Little John, the hour bell in its dome, weighs over 10 tonnes, and its strike can be heard 7 miles away.[^s1][^s1]

From 1283 the borough of Nottingham sent two members to Parliament. In the mid-18th century the great landowners, the Duke of Newcastle for the Whigs and Lord Middleton for the Tories, held sway, and the town usually returned one of each. In 1885 the old two-member seat was abolished, and the city was divided into three seats of one member each: Nottingham East, South and West.
The architect Thomas Cecil Howitt designed the Council House.[^s1][^s2]

74840.sum: The Nottingham Council House is the former city hall of Nottingham, England. The 200 feet high dome that rises above the city is the centrepiece of the skyline and presides over the Old Market Square, which is also referred to as the "City Centre". The building is Grade II* listed, and has retail units at street-level.

stories.text: Built for the lace manufacturers John and William Lambert, who wanted a prestigious theatre for the town, to designs by Charles J. Phipps; its portico of six Corinthian columns closes the view up Market Street. It opened on 25 September 1865 with Sheridan's The School for Scandal, and in 1897 Frank Matcham remodelled its auditorium. In October 1952 it staged the world premiere of Agatha Christie's The Mousetrap.
The theatre architect Charles J. Phipps designed the Theatre Royal.[^s1][^s2]

74992.sum: The Theatre Royal in Nottingham, England, is a theatre venue in the heart of Nottingham City Centre and is owned by Nottingham City Council as part of a complex that also includes the city's Royal Concert Hall. The Theatre Royal attracts major touring dramas, opera, ballet, West End musicals and an annual pantomime.

stories.text: In 1898 Frank Matcham designed and built the Empire Palace of Varieties here. It closed for the last time in 1958 and was demolished for road-widening in 1969. On 27 November 1982 the Royal Concert Hall, designed by the Renton Howard Wood Levin Partnership, opened on the site, with Elton John as its first performer.

74994.sum: Nottingham Royal Concert Hall is a concert hall in the English city of Nottingham. It is owned by Nottingham City Council and is part of a complex that also includes the city's Theatre Royal. The Royal Concert Hall's striking modern architecture has proved to be a city landmark at the heart of Nottingham City Centre, opposite the more recently built The Cornerhouse complex.

stories.text: Built in 1887–88 to designs by Thomas Verity and George Henry Hunt, chosen in a competition judged by Alfred Waterhouse, it replaced the old Guild Hall on Weekday Cross and served as the city's magistrates' court. The council used it as offices until 2010; it has stood largely empty since.

74995.sum: Nottingham Guildhall is a former magistrates' court in Nottingham, England. The structure, which was used by Nottingham City Council as offices in the 1990s, is a Grade II listed building.
